newsitem.title: USA: Miami, Fla., declares fiscal emergency.
newsitem.headline: Miami, Fla., declares fiscal emergency.

text.p: The City of Miami, Fla., said Monday it had declared a fiscal emergency, citing a budget gap increase to $68 million for fiscal 1997, which began October 1.

In addition, the city said the city commission voted unanimously to dismiss outside auditor Deloitte Touche because the accounting firm allegedly did not provide adequate warning to the city about the budget problems.
The city also said it will investigate possible legal action against the firm for alleged malpractice.
The emergency declaration will allow the city to reopen contracts with its four employee unions.
Acting city manager Merrett Stierheim said the city would first seek $50 million in voluntary concessions from the unions before attempting to reopen contracts.
He said the city would also seek to raise fees by $14 million, to cut services by $3 million and seek pension cost reductions of $6 million to help offset the budget short fall.
He said the city would also explore lease-backed agreements, federal and state grants and the sale of unneeded assets to help close the budget gap.
